newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC says no plans for Hang Seng Bank stake change.
newsitem.headline: HSBC says no plans for Hang Seng Bank stake change.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc had no plans to change its shareholding in subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd, an HSBC spokeswoman said on Friday.
"Hang Seng is our long term holding, we have no plan to change our holding in Hang Seng Bank," the spokeswoman said.
HSBC Holdings holds about 63.6 percent of Hang Seng Bank as in May 1997.
Shares in Hang Seng Bank surged on speculation that the bank might be a possible acquisition target by mainland Chinese firms and on rumours that a Chinese firm might take a stake.
The spokeswoman declined to comment on the speculation.
"We are not commenting on market rumours," she said.

Hang Seng Bank said in a statement on Friday it was not aware of any reason for the share price rise and said there were no disclosable negotiations or agreements relating to intended acquisitions or realisations.
Hang Seng Bank shares rose HK$9.25 to an all time high of HK$106 in mid-morning. HSBC shares rose HK$5.00 to HK$231.
